llm.summary: The skill is mostly a coherent Lokalise connector, but its setup instructions include unverified remote installer commands that can execute mutable code on the user’s machine.

dimensions.detail: Normal runtime authority is limited to Bash(oo *) and the skill says credentials are injected server-side, which is proportionate for a connector skill; the installer instructions are the main overbroad environment risk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: First-time setup instructs macOS/Linux users to run curl piped to bash and Windows users to pipe a remote PowerShell script to iex, without pinning or integrity verification.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The description broadly routes any Lokalise request to this skill, but the runtime scope remains Lokalise-specific and the instructions require user confirmation for write and destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses one-time CLI installation, authentication, and account connection steps, with no bundled persistent code or hidden services found in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill’s purpose and capabilities align: it operates Lokalise through the OOMOL oo CLI and clearly lists read, write, and destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable using OOMOL as the intermediary for Lokalise actions and avoid running the documented curl|bash or irm|iex installer commands unless you independently trust and verify the oo CLI installer source. Review all write or delete payloads before approval.
llm.findings:
[SC2] expected: Installing the oo CLI is purpose-related fallback setup, but the artifact-backed pipe-to-shell installer instructions create a material supply-chain concern.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad Lokalise routing is expected for a service-specific connector and is partly mitigated by explicit read/write/destructive labeling and confirmation requirements.
[T03] expected: The static finding matches the actual setup commands; there is no evidence the remote installer is malicious, but executing mutable remote scripts without verification warrants Review.
